entries.title: Resolve required capabilities from one process-live target truth
entries.competitorOutcome: Firebase, Supabase, Convex, Appwrite, and SpacetimeDB admitted their ordinary authenticated Research Room application with realtime scheduled progress; Snapback's exact runtime implements the stream but its sessions cold-start path refuses the composition.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Complete-pair pre-effect startup admission, server-derived sessions authority, fail-closed capability requirements, and the instance-live registered-implementation plus egress predicate.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: Cold-start preflight, same-mode provisioning, ordinary publication, generated manifests, and served inspection resolve every required capability from the same exact process-live target facts.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A clean external sessions application requiring bounded_response_stream_v1 cold-starts only when this exact process enables outbound actions; two sessions observe durable intermediate progress, cancellation fences late writes, all terminal outcomes remain distinct, and the egress-disabled twin refuses before bind.

entries.title: Ship an authenticated asset lifecycle instead of metadata-only rows
entries.competitorOutcome: Five competitors provided native byte upload, authorized member delivery, owner deletion, and post-delete absence without relabeling application metadata as storage.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Server-derived authority, target portability, export/restore legibility, bounded resource use, and exact cleanup.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: A declared asset field or resource supports bounded byte upload, authority-scoped delivery, ownership, deletion, export/restore, and target-reported limits through generated clients.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Partiful and Research Room upload deterministic fixtures, prove member byte identity and outsider refusal, enforce owner deletion, restore/export identity, and clean every byte from a target-scoped namespace.

entries.title: Make authorized indexed text and semantic retrieval ordinary
entries.competitorOutcome: Supabase and Convex supplied indexed full-text plus native vector retrieval in the same data authority; Firebase supplied a credible provider-native semantic extension path, while Appwrite and InstantDB made their vector gaps explicit.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Authorization is evaluated with retrieval, results remain target-portable and inspectable, deterministic fixtures are possible, and scans are never mislabeled as indexes.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: Schema declarations can opt into authorized full-text and vector similarity indexes with generated query forms, explicit target capability admission, and honest per-target gaps.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Linear returns exact indexed keyword sets under member/outsider authority; Research Room returns the deterministic nearest authorized source from a native vector query; unsupported targets refuse at admission rather than scanning.

entries.title: Bring protected offline retention and queued settlement to ordinary clients
entries.competitorOutcome: Firebase and InstantDB expose retained data and reconnect settlement through their normal application clients rather than a benchmark-only or custom sync path.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Lease-bounded protected bytes, user-switch deletion, server authority, explicit conflict and ambiguity, and replay parity.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: Generated clients expose opt-in protected cold retention and a restart-safe outbox with visible cache provenance and exact settlement.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A cold client renders only still-leased rows, queues a mutation across restart, settles exactly once after reconnect, exposes conflicts, and deletes or quarantines protected bytes on expiry, logout, revocation, and principal switch.

entries.title: Make a hosted deployment an evidence-bearing ordinary path
entries.competitorOutcome: Managed competitors offer an ordinary hosted target identity and deployment workflow; local-first competitors at least make the hosted gap and lifecycle legible.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Local completeness, portable artifacts, exact deployment identity, scoped authority, rollback, backup, and no hidden control-plane trust.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: A clean external project can deploy the same admitted artifact to a named hosted target and inspect identity, region, version, auth posture, logs, backup/export, rollback, cost scope, and exact cleanup.
entries.acceptanceWitness: All five frozen apps deploy from clean external projects; target identities match served inspection, smoke and rollback pass, backup/read-back is byte exact, costs are scoped, and deletion leaves no app namespace.

entries.title: Make clean external-project bootstrap boring
entries.competitorOutcome: Convex, Firebase, InstantDB, and SpacetimeDB can reach their ordinary local or temporary-hosted loop from published CLIs and packages without repository-internal source knowledge.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: The local target remains the complete runtime, prepared artifacts are verified, source build remains explicit, and binary provenance is inspectable.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: A supported clean machine creates, generates, builds, starts, verifies, and removes an external Snapback app through one documented package path without a sibling checkout or implicit Hermes build.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Fresh macOS and Linux machines with empty caches run the published quickstart and all five final Snapback arms; binary/package identity is independently verified and no repository-relative import appears.

entries.title: Teach outbound capability admission at compile time and runtime
entries.competitorOutcome: Integrated function providers make the build/deploy boundary for external effects visible in their ordinary function workflow and return phase-specific diagnostics.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Egress stays opt-in, generated requirements cannot grant target authority, diagnostics remain value-free, and unsupported targets refuse before effects.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The Guide and diagnostics distinguish authoring/codegen declaration from process-live target admission, show the grant on every relevant command, and prove their composition in sessions mode.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A clean documented fetch/stream example generates and runs with the gate enabled; codegen-disabled and runtime-disabled twins fail with different actionable value-free diagnostics; Guide snippets are CI-verified.

entries.title: Put bounded mutation limits and bulk-import guidance before runtime
entries.competitorOutcome: Competitors expose batch, transaction, or import limits close to the ordinary bulk-write path, reducing discovery through production-shaped failure.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Atomic mutation buffering remains bounded and deterministic; larger imports do not silently weaken transaction or authority semantics.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The mutation Guide states the exact target-reported ceiling, what counts as one buffered write, and a bounded resumable import pattern.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A CI-verified example imports more than one mutation ceiling in bounded chunks, resumes without duplicates, and an over-limit mutation retains SNAPBACK_BUFFERED_WRITE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

entries.title: Pave multi-principal sessions tests and anonymous public reads
entries.competitorOutcome: Firebase, Supabase, Convex, Appwrite, and InstantDB provide ordinary test identities and public/authenticated client paths without hand-authoring protocol headers or discovering mailbox custody through source.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: The server derives identity, mailbox and impersonation authority never enter browser code, anonymous calls cannot smuggle principals, and reset revokes prior authority.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: First-party test helpers create multiple genuine local sessions; generated/headless clients expose an admitted anonymous public mode; the Guide teaches reset-safe membership bootstrap.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A clean sessions demo creates Alice, Bob, and Mallory through a server-side helper, serves an anonymous public preview and protected controls through paved clients, proves outsider denial, and survives a reset using authenticated resource bootstrap.

entries.title: Expose honest GAPs for assets and notification delivery in the capability index
entries.competitorOutcome: Competitors document Storage and notification/function surfaces directly; builders can decide before modeling whether the integrated product covers bytes and delivery.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Capability claims remain target-specific, evidence-backed, and explicit about missing surfaces; metadata rows and effect ledgers are not mislabeled.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The complete capability index contains owned, dated assets and notification-delivery GAP rows linked to governing work and current non-goals.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Guide search reaches both rows, the Guide checker validates their metadata, and an agent reading only the index correctly predicts the Partiful and Research Room outcomes.

entries.title: Provide a typed local configuration automation path
entries.competitorOutcome: Integrated function providers expose a first-party CLI or management API for setting opaque runtime configuration and inspecting presence without returning values.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Values never appear in manifests, argv, logs, browser memory, status output, or committed fixtures; generation and pool semantics stay explicit.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The privileged headless client or CLI exposes typed status, set, unset, and verify operations with generation handling and value-free receipts.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A clean local demo follows only the Guide to set, verify, use, rotate, and remove an Action canary; exact-value scans of source, argv, logs, receipts, browser state, and final target are zero.

entries.title: Keep explicit effect certainty and cancellation fencing first-class
entries.competitorOutcome: Competitors often reach scheduled progress quickly but require application-authored state machines to distinguish failed, cancelled, timed-out, and ambiguous effects and to fence late writes.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Host-derived effect certainty, durable terminal winners, conflict reconciliation, and no late durable patch after cancellation.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: Improve the ergonomics and generated patterns around Snapback's existing settlement model rather than replacing it with provider-shaped best-effort retries.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Partiful and Research Room retain distinct terminal states, exact effectMayHaveExecuted facts, authoritative intermediate push, idempotent rejoin, and zero late patches under cancellation and timeout.

entries.title: Put membership-command cardinality beside the generated authoring path
entries.competitorOutcome: Competitor membership setup APIs either accepted the frozen multi-member seed or exposed their transaction/resource boundary before the application ran.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Each generated membership command remains an explicit fail-closed authority transition; several commands never become accidentally atomic or partially applied inside one mutation.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The Guide and, where statically visible, codegen state the one-command v1 ceiling, bootstrap expansion, exact refusal, and an idempotent multi-mutation setup pattern.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A documented Research Room setup creates two resources and two member grants through four idempotent calls; a one-mutation four-command twin refuses atomically with SNAPBACK_MEMBERSHIP_BATCH_UNSUPPORTED.

entries.title: Make public client inspection negotiate the active sessions profile
entries.competitorOutcome: Competitor client diagnostics and emulator inspection paths remain usable under the same ordinary authentication profile as application calls.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Public served facts and sensitive operator facts remain separate; the secret-read lease is never inferred from an application session.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: SnapbackClient.inspect negotiates the active public auth-client protocol automatically while sensitive operator inspection retains its distinct typed authorization.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A sessions client reads public /inspect through the official method without hand-authored headers, receives a typed refusal for operator inspection without a secret-read lease, and succeeds only after minting that lease.
